title: Life cycle of stack memory
concept: Variables (local variables) created within a function disappear when the function ends.

steps.title: Include stdio.h header
steps.explanation: Standard input/output header for use with ``printf````. In this lesson, we cover **the life cycle of functions and the life of local variables** — you will directly observe what happens when a function is called and what disappears when it ends.

steps.title: func function blueprint
steps.explanation:
`func` is a function definition (design) step, not executable code.

Actual stack frame creation and execution occurs at the time of the `func();` call.

steps.title: Start program execution
steps.explanation:
When a program starts, the main stack frame is created first.

It operates according to the LIFO structure, where frames are pushed when a function is called and popped when the function ends.

steps.title: func() function call (Push)
steps.explanation:
When you call `func();`, the stack frame of `func` is pushed onto main.

Since a separate frame is created for each function call, the local variables of each function are stored in different memory spaces.

steps.title: Creating local variables in func
steps.explanation:
A local variable `a` is created within the `func` frame. This variable is only valid inside `func`.

`a` cannot be accessed directly from main.

steps.title: Output inside func
steps.explanation:
Check the func local variable value and address with `printf`.

This address is only valid while the func frame is alive and should not be trusted after the function exits.

steps.title: exit func() function (Pop)
steps.explanation:
When func ends, the func stack frame is popped and local variables lose their scope as well.

Therefore, it is dangerous to continue to use the address of local variables inside a function outside of the function.

steps.title: return to main
steps.explanation:
When `func` finishes, the `func` frame is popped and control returns to main.

At this time, the local variables of `func` are destroyed, and only the variables of main remain.
steps.stdout:
Inside func: 10, Addr: 0x...
Back in main

steps.title: exit main function
steps.explanation:
`return 0;` ends main and any remaining stack frames are cleaned up.

The key is the stack frame flow, which is pushed when called and popped when terminated.

quiz.question: In which memory area are local variables within a function stored?
quiz.explanation:
Local variables and parameters are stored in the Stack area.
It appears when a function is called (Push) and disappears when it is finished (Pop).

misconceptions.wrong: Even after the function ends, the variable value remains in memory.
misconceptions.correct: It cannot be accessed and will soon be overwritten.
misconceptions.why:
As the stack pointer shrinks, the space is treated as 'empty space'.
It will be reused in the next function call.

keyTakeaway: The lifetime of a local variable is the same as the lifetime of the function. After the function is over, you have to leave the room.
